title: Worst-Case Calibration of Pairwise-Imputation Randomization Tests under Interference
banked_reason: Cold general referee: delivered tier=subfield below field floor with paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4; scalable certified computation beyond Cycle5 or the common s=0 frontier would be required to lift it.
gap_reasons: Its operational contribution remains limited by exhaustive chamber enumeration: beyond the five-assignment cycle, it supplies neither a scalable certified implementation nor evidence that design-specific calibration can be computed for practically relevant supports.

The universal lower frontier is obtained through increasingly large, deliberately engineered positive-radius tournament designs and does not settle the common zero-radius subclass, whose sharp constant and thresholdwise frontier remain open.

The comparator table calls the result equivalent to Li--Zhou--Zhang (2026, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2), but that source establishes sharpness for grouped PALMRT in a fixed-design regression/permutation model, whereas this theorem's claimed contribution is a legal distance-interference, complete-randomization, fixed-score realization; replace the equivalence label with an explicit same-bound/different-model comparison and state that neither theorem subsumes the other.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the exact finite-design calibration envelope, rational realizability certificates, structural C*=1 and C*=4/3 examples, and legal tournament constructions proving the sharp thresholdwise factor-two frontier. The mathematics passed review, but the package remained subfield-level because scalable certified computation beyond Cycle5 and the common s=0 frontier remain open research programs; one comparator-relation prose correction also remains.
tldr: For Zhong's standard near-minus-pure-control pairwise-imputation randomization test, legal null comparison arrays are exactly rationally feasible chambers of a design-determined hyperplane arrangement, yielding the exact pointwise-minimal monotone envelope \(F_*\). Equal-clique designs have \(C_*=1\), and the audited five-cycle has \(C_*=4/3\). Over the legal positive-radius fixed-score tournament subclass, and therefore over Zhong's full finite PIRT class, the exact across-design frontier at every fixed \(u\in(0,1]\) is \(\sup F_*(u)/u=\min\{2,1/u\}\). At \(0<u\leq1/2\) this value is approached from below but is never attained by an individual finite positive-mass design. A scalable certified algorithm beyond the five-cycle and the corresponding \(s=0\) frontier remain open.
gap: The published comparison-matrix argument explains a generic factor-two safeguard, but it does not use the restrictions imposed by joint imputability, fixed treatment count, distance exposure groups, or Zhong's fixed score. Existing conditional interference tests solve nonsharpness by selecting sharp subexperiments rather than calibrating this unconditional p-value.
fill: The proposal seeks to characterize realizability by rational primal and dual certificates, derive and certify the least monotone envelope, give structural exactness and nonexact examples, and determine the universal legal constant. Scalable certified computation and the \(s=0\) frontier remain explicit questions rather than promised solved conclusions.
